messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging eng-oncall — elevated 500s on /v1/generate (us-east-1). Alerting from load-balancer and metric anomalies. Full symptom set: high p95 latency, 5xx burst, some client timeouts.
Samir: Got the page, joining. I'm on call now.
Maya: I'm looking at the proxy logs — seeing a sharp increase in upstream 503s coming from embed-service nodes. Noted ~10:12 -> 10:25 spike.
Jordan: I can repro with a localized load test script against a subset of hosts. Trying to curl a few backends.
Priya: Customer success flagged a handful of customers experiencing failures during that window — escalated some PMs. I'm drafting a status note.
Luca: Copy. Can we triage whether this is routing or backend overload?
Maya: backend oom patterns in kube events on node gke-us-east-1a-12. Logs show repeated KV cache miss storms followed by mem pressure.
Anya: Pushing a quick mitigation: scaling the embed-service HPA from 6 -> 12 to relieve KV pressure. Doing a canary scale first.
Jordan: Rolling a temporary routing rule to divert 20% traffic to the smaller-quantized model variant to reduce GPU memory per-request. Command: `kubectl apply -f /ops/routing/temp-divert-20.yaml`
Samir: On it — I just applied the routing patch and confirmed new requests are flowing to model-small. Observed error rate drop within ~90s.
incident-bot: (automated) Incident tagged: INC-2026-0421; severity: sev2. Channels: #incidents, #eng-oncall.
Priya: Notifying affected customers with preliminary ETA: mitigation in progress. Sending an interim note to the client list now.
Maya: After scale and routing change, node memory reclaim succeeded. I see decreased OOM events. Post-change p95 latency improved from 1.8s -> 0.9s.
Jordan: Confirmed — no new 5xxs in the last 8 minutes on diverted traffic. Original pool still seeing intermittent errors; looks like cache cold-starts amplified under load.
Anya: Action item: enable prefix caching on the embed path for aggressive TTL for 6 hours to smooth cold starts. I'll open a follow-up ticket.
Samir: Agree. Also recommend we add a conservative circuit-breaker rule to route to model-small if per-instance rps > 120 for 30s. Will create the runtime policy PR.
Priya: Customer comms sent — included note about temporary routing and that we'll follow up with a full postmortem.
Luca: Good. We should schedule a postmortem this week. Who wants to lead? Volunteers: Maya (root cause on nodes), Jordan (mitigation owner), Samir (oncall timeline).
Maya: I can lead the postmortem write-up. Suggest Thursday 16:00 ET for a 45-min retro.
Jordan: I'll co-author mitigation timeline and include the k8s events + `kubectl describe` snippets.
Anya: I'll take action items for instrumentation: add a metric for KV miss storm rate and an alert when miss_rate > 0.2 for 1m.
Samir: I'll file the ops-runbook update for routing fallback and attach the PR link in the postmortem.
Priya: I'll follow up with customer impact summary and include affected orgs and tickets.
Luca: Assign owners and Jira IDs during the meeting. Proposed agenda: 1) Timeline & detection 2) Root cause 3) Mitigations (temporary + long-term) 4) Action items + owners 5) Brown-bag shareout plan.
Maya: For the timeline, here's the quick snippet I'll include in the doc:
```
10:11 - LB alerts spike in 5xx
10:12 - incident-bot page triggered
10:13 - Samir acknowledged oncall
10:14 - initial triage finds embed-service 503s
10:17 - Jordan starts routing diversion to model-small
10:19 - scale-up start HPA 6->12
10:21 - mem reclaim observed; 5xxs begin dropping
10:35 - stable; rotate to monitoring
```
Jordan: Also adding the mitigation commands used in case we need runbook updates:
```
kubectl apply -f /ops/routing/temp-divert-20.yaml
kubectl scale hpa/embed-service --replicas=12
kubectl logs -n embed svc/embed-abc -c embed | tail -n 200
```
Anya: For long-term prevention I propose: 1) KV cache TTL tuning + pre-warm caches on deploy, 2) circuit-breaker policies, 3) extended autoscaler cooldowns, 4) canary traffic ramp to detect cold-start amplification.
Samir: Add a postmortem checklist item to run a replay load test against a canary scaled-down cluster to validate fallback rules. I'll own the test.
Priya: Can we also plan a 30-min brown-bag training for Platform and SRE teams to surface this pattern (cold-start + cache storms) and runbook changes? Proposed date: next Tuesday 11:00 PT.
Luca: Yes — schedule brown-bag and include a short demo of the routing fallback and how to read the KV metrics. Maya and Jordan to present.
Maya: I'll prepare slides on root cause and mitigation; Jordan will demo the runbook commands.
Anya: I'll include the new dashboard mockups for the KV-miss metric and demo queries.
Samir: Created initial Jira: INFRA-4321 (Postmortem: embed-service 5xx storm). I'll attach owners and link to this thread.
Priya: Adding customer-ticket refs: CUST-9981, CUST-9988 to the postmortem doc.
Luca: Next steps: Maya to publish draft postmortem by Wednesday EOD, Samir to add runbook PR, Anya to create alert + dashboard, Jordan to prepare mitigation artifacts, Priya to consolidate customer impact. We'll meet Thursday 16:00 ET.
Samir: Thanks team — big win getting errors down fast. Let's make the follow-ups concrete and preserve the mitigation knobs in the runbook. :thumbsup:
Priya: I'll post the calendar invite and add the doc link once Maya starts the draft.
incident-bot: (automated) Reminder set: postmortem-draft-due Wednesday EOD.
Maya: Draft started -> https://docs.internal.redwood/postmortems/INFRA-4321 (will add timeline + logs).
Anya: Creating dashboard PR: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/kv-miss/kv-miss-dashboard (WIP).
Jordan: I'll upload the exact `curl` reproducer and k8s event exports to the doc after the meeting.
Luca: Thanks all — we'll close the thread once postmortem is published and brown-bag is scheduled.
Priya: Closing loop: customers updated, tickets linked. Good job.
Samir: ccing next shift oncall in case follow-ups trigger alerts: @Anya (next oncall).
Anya: Got it, standing by for postmortem review.
Maya: End of thread — preparing slides now.
